subject: Post-demo calibration: Glyph pilot TCO probe & 1M-token bench asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@glyph.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo calibration: Glyph pilot TCO probe & 1M-token bench asks

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for taking the demo with us today. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can operationalize the competitive/TCO comparison you requested. High-level notes from the call:

- Glyph priority: predictable unit cost for inference at 1M tokens scale, and latency must be under 200ms p99 for interactive flows.
- You asked for apples-to-apples numbers vs the major hyperscaler you evaluated and an actual run we can analyze (not just theoretical math).

What we can provide immediately:
- A short 1M-token benchmark run using your production prompt mix (we'll replay up to 1,000,000 tokens).
- A batch-sensitivity sweep (batch sizes: 1, 4, 16) to show per-token delta and latency tradeoffs.
- Cache-hit scenarios: 0%, ~30%, and ~60% to show the impact of prefix/KV caching on unit cost.

To set expectations from our side (hosted API numbers, rough order of magnitude):
- Redwood hosted (with batching + prefix cache): ~$7.8 per 1M tokens (typical mix, avg seq ~512) at ~60% cache hit; p95 latencies ~90–120ms with moderate batches.
- Hyperscaler (public numbers you shared): list price equivalent ~$5.6 per 1M tokens but assumes no KV/prefix cache, higher p95 latencies and additional networking egress for multi-region failover; effective delivered cost often higher once you include polling/latency retry overheads.
- Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) can push per-1M to the low-$3s depending on commit and utilization.

Asks / next steps:
1) Confirm you want us to run the 1M-token replay against production prompt samples (we need a small sample set or the replay payload).
2) Confirm the average sequence length to target (we used 512 in the demo; if Glyph's median is <256 or >1024, tell us).
3) Share any strict latency SLOs we should try to hit in the test.
4) If procurement needs a formal SOW / pilot agreement, we can circulate a short DocuSign pilot (2-week run + pilot credits) — attached a draft pilot agreement and a CSV with the test matrix.

Attachments: redwood-glyph-bench-ask-20280402.csv (test matrix stub), pilot-agreement.docx (draft), reference cost table (inline).

If that plan looks good I can kick off the bench tomorrow morning and share raw logs + a short readout.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick recap. A few clarifications before we sign off on the test matrix:

1) Sequence length: our real traffic is bimodal — ~55% short (avg 64 tokens), ~45% long (avg ~768). Can you do a mixed replay representing those proportions?
2) Cache behavior: we rely heavily on a 3-turn context reuse across sessions; how do you simulate that in the cache scenarios?
3) Procurement: procurement@glyph.ai wants to see a pilot agreement and a short list of compliance artifacts (SOC2 in-scope items). We attached our pilot requirements PDF.

We can provide a sanitized prompt sample set and a signed NDA if needed.

If you can scope the mixed traffic replay and include short/long percentiles in the readout, we’ll schedule the replay for this Thurs (4/5).

Thanks —
Ethan

- Ask Eng to capture: per-token CPU/GPU cycles (approx), batch size vs p95 latency, and cache-hit delta on per-1M cost. These three metrics will land the cost argument.
